messages:
morgan: trying to repro the perf regression we saw this morning — kernels keep flipping and KV cache eviction spikes. planning an nsys capture. anyone have a concise set of CLI flags that capture: cuda kernels, NVTX ranges for our warmup bracket, and OSRT markers, but keep sampling so the file stays small? :thinking:

morgan: want to capture the kernel timeline + nvtx brackets around batching decisions. goal: 30s capture with warmup bracket and sample-based profiling to avoid 10GB trace files.

devon: i'd do bracketed capture using NVTX markers from the code (push/pop around warmup and critical sections) + nsys sampling. quick example i use:```
nsys profile --output=tmp/nv_capture --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu,cuda --sample-freq=10000 --capture-range=nvtx:WARMUP_START,nvtx:WARMUP_END --target-pid 23456 --duration=30
```
This keeps the timeline focused and sampling keeps file size down. adjust --sample-freq if you need finer grain.

lia: two more gotchas: 1) when you use OSRT with sampling, include osrt in --trace (you already have) but ensure your runtime emits the osrt markers consistently — otherwise brackets look empty. 2) if you're chasing kernel selection, add --cuda-memory-usage to see memcpy overlapped patterns (helps spot prefetch vs evict).

samir: also consider splitting capture into two short runs instead of one long one: warmup bracket (15s) + steady-state (15s) with different sample rates. i usually:```
# warmup (higher sample to catch short kernels)
nsys profile --output=warmup --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu,cuda --sample-freq=20000 --capture-range=nvtx:WARMUP_START,nvtx:WARMUP_END --target-pid 23456 --duration=15

# steady (lower sample to reduce size)
nsys profile --output=steady --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu,cuda --sample-freq=8000 --capture-range=nvtx:STEADY_START,nvtx:STEADY_END --target-pid 23456 --duration=15
```
Splitting also helps compare kernel selection changes across windows.

devon: one more — if the trace still balloons, filter by process and by CUDA device index: `--target-pid` and `--cuda-device 0`. avoids noisy system activity from other containers.

lia: and if you're seeing KV-cache thrash specifically, add a small NVTX annotation in the runtime where we evict/prefetch so the timeline shows correlation:```
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("kvcache:prefetch")
...prefetch code...
NVTX_RANGE_POP()
```
That makes it trivial to eyeball if evict correlates with kernel switches.

morgan: awesome, will try split runs + NVTX markers. curious — any preferred post-capture workflow? i usually open the .nsys-rep and go to the timeline + kernel view, then export a CSV of GPU kernel events.

samir: export CSV + callstack sampling view. look for lots of short kernel spikes (~<200us) — that usually indicates we're hitting a different kernel variant per batch size. if you see repeated memcpy + tiny kernel pairs, we may be re-shuffling KV cache.

ops-bot: nsys capture saved: /artifacts/nvsaves/nv_capture_warmup_4498761234.qdrep (size: 312MB) — use `nsys stats` to quickly get top kernels.

morgan: got the warmup file, looks ~300MB. starting steady run now with --sample-freq=8000 and target-pid 23456. will post quick findings in a follow-up. :+1:
